contract_plain_english: For a Poisson random variable X with parameter lambda, Stirling's formula gives the large-k approximation P{X=k} approximately equal to exp(-lambda)(e lambda/k)^k divided by sqrt(2 pi k). When k is the first integer in the relevant upper tail, the exponential term is the same as the Poisson upper-tail bound from (2.8), so that bound differs from the probability of even one tail value only by the square-root factor sqrt(2 pi k). The source therefore calls the bound quite sharp on the exponential scale, while leaving the approximation error, the precise limiting regime, and the real-threshold-to-integer correspondence implicit.
